address_spaces.name: cached
address_spaces.notes: The cached xkphys base, with no attribute; the same value as the Origin 200.

address_spaces.name: Hub special
address_spaces.notes: Attribute 0, as on the Origin 200. Split on IP35 into a 128 MB local register window at 0x1000_0000 and a 128 MB boot window at 0x1800_0000, with remote forms at 0x3000_0000 and 0x3800_0000. The L1 UART is inside the register window. The OpenBSD board-identification read remains an unresolved consumer requirement.

address_spaces.name: I/O
address_spaces.notes: 16 MB small windows at widget times 16 MB; 512 MB big windows in M mode at (entry plus one) times 512 MB, selected by seven translation entries; the Bedrock's own registers are widget 1 of the node.

address_spaces.name: uncached memory
address_spaces.notes: Attribute 3. The node number sits at physical bits 39:33 in M mode, seven bits, an 8 GB node window and 128 nodes; N mode halves the window and is out of scope.

machine.name: Origin 3900
machine.notes: The smallest Origin 3900 partition: one Cx-brick with all four IP53 node boards fitted, sixteen processors, and an I-brick on node board 0's XIO connector at its XBridge port A. Node board 0 and port A are this composition's choices; which XIO connector a boot I-brick uses is unknown. An IX-brick may take the I-brick's place on a real partition; no IX-brick layer exists yet. No source fixes the Cx-brick's processor clock, part, reset mode, node-board part, Bedrock revision, router port per node board, NASID base, XIO widget numbers or memory. Each node board is fitted as the Origin 350's IP53 is (four 700 MHz R16000 processors with 8 MB secondary caches, its reset mode and 2048 MB in banks 0 and 1), the Bedrock is the 200 MHz revision 2 every published inventory reports, and node board n takes router port n+2; all are approximations the Cx-brick datasheet lists. The boards are numbered NASID 0 to 3 by board number, where the Origin 3900 guide orders them board 1, 2, 0, 3 from an unknown base, so the model's NASIDs differ from the figure's. The Cx-brick's L1 reports the C-brick's type character, an approximation the stock PROM needs to name the module. The router answers the model's synthetic diagnostics, which no hardware record settles. The rack's L2 controller is not modelled.

variants.notes: The Origin 3200 C-brick's selected fit. Established: a posted Origin 3200 inventory reports four 400 MHz R12000s per C-brick at revision 3.5, each with an 8 MB secondary cache at 266 MHz, and an R12010 FPU at revision 3.5. Inferred: the PRId and the FPU identification, from those printed revisions and the R10000-family implementation numbers. Approximated: the reset-mode word is the low 25 bits of the stock IP35 PROM's configuration-table word for a 400 MHz, 8 MB C-brick, the way the Origin 300's R14000 word is its row's; no capture of a C-brick's reset mode exists.

variants.notes: QEMU's currently shipping 500 MHz/2 MiB Origin 300 configuration writes this exact Config0 low-25-bit reset word (readback 0x6c9aa985). No product here yet reads this field; it moves machine.firmware_config.processor_reset_mode here for a future compiler once a Bedrock-node compile path exists.
